The sector area is 3π/4. If P=(p,0), the semicircle radius is (3−p)/2 and its center is ((p+3)/2,0); its distance to OB is (p+3)/4. Tangency gives p=1 and radius 1, so S₂=π/2 and total 5π/4. Opened diagram confirms the semicircle is tangent to OB.
Set t=nx, so t spans [0,2n²π], containing n² full periods and two roots per period. Thus f(n)=2n²≤270 and the largest integer n is 11.

From f(x)=2^x−1 and g(x)=log₂(x+1), A=(0,0), and their common point with x=1 is D=(1,1). B=(3,7) from f(3)=7; C=(3,2) from g(x)=2⇒x=3. Thus [ADC]=|1·2−1·3|/2=1/2. For DBC, BC=5 and the horizontal distance from D to x=3 is 2, so [DBC]=5·2/2=5. The sum is 11/2, the second choice. The five listed choices are distinct; exactly one equals 11/2.
The domain requires x>3/2. Since the base 3 is increasing, the inequality is equivalent to (x−1)/((2/3)x−1)>3, which reduces to x<2. Hence αβ=(3/2)·2=3.

The radius equation gives |y_Q|=1/3; Q is on the lower branch, so −log_a3=−1/3, yielding a=27. Opened diagram agrees with the lower-right point Q.

For b=1, the relevant powers of 2 are 1 and 2, giving sin(aπx)=−1 and 0. The zero level contributes a+1 roots and the −1 level contributes floor(a/2) roots, so exactly 7 occurs at a=4. For b≥2 the only possible power level in [2b−1,2b+1] is 2b when that is a power of 2, corresponding to sin(aπx)=0; this contributes a+1 roots, so a=6. The distinct a values sum to 10.
